common_name: Primal Scream Daylily (Award-Winning Vivid Orange-Red Daylily)

planting.note: Plant divisions in spring in well-drained, moderately fertile soil in full sun; Primal Scream is an award-winning daylily cultivar known for large, intensely saturated orange-red flowers with a darker eye zone, blooming heavily over a long midsummer season.

directions: Plant in well-drained, moderately fertile soil in full sun. Primal Scream is a widely acclaimed daylily cultivar bearing large, ruffled, intensely saturated orange-red flowers accented by a darker red eye zone and a bright yellow-green throat, a bold color combination that reads vividly even from a distance. It received the American Hemerocallis Society's Stout Silver Medal, the organization's highest honor, in recognition of its outstanding garden performance, vigorous growth, and heavy, reliable bloom production over a long midsummer season. The strong, well-branched scapes hold plenty of buds for an extended flowering display, and the plant multiplies steadily into a robust, floriferous clump. Like other daylilies it is easy to grow in average soil with routine watering, tolerating heat and a range of soil conditions well. Divide congested clumps every three to four years in spring or fall to maintain vigor and bloom quality.

common_name: Bela Lugosi Daylily (Deep Purple-Black Award-Winning Daylily)

planting.note: Plant divisions in spring in well-drained, moderately fertile soil in full sun; Bela Lugosi is an award-winning daylily cultivar with large, deep purple-black flowers and a contrasting green throat, among the darkest-colored daylilies widely available.

directions: Plant in well-drained, moderately fertile soil in full sun. Bela Lugosi is a striking daylily cultivar, named for the classic horror-film actor, bearing large, ruffled flowers in one of the deepest, darkest purples available in the genus, verging on black in certain light, with a vivid chartreuse-green throat that provides sharp contrast. It received the American Hemerocallis Society's Stout Silver Medal for its exceptional garden performance and distinctive, richly colored blooms produced over a long midsummer season on tall, sturdy scapes. The dramatic dark coloring makes it an outstanding focal point in a mixed perennial border, especially paired with lighter-colored companion plants for contrast. Like other daylilies it is easy to grow in average soil with routine watering and tolerates heat well. Divide congested clumps every three to four years in spring or fall to maintain vigor and bloom quality.

common_name: Strawberry Candy Daylily (Pink Reblooming Daylily with Rose Eye)

planting.note: Plant divisions in spring in well-drained, moderately fertile soil in full sun; Strawberry Candy is a popular, widely grown reblooming daylily with rose-pink flowers marked by a deeper raspberry-rose eye zone, valued for its vigor, heavy rebloom, and ease of growth.

directions: Plant in well-drained, moderately fertile soil in full sun. Strawberry Candy is one of the most widely planted modern daylily cultivars, bearing bright rose-pink flowers with a distinct, deeper raspberry-rose eye zone and a matching ruffled edge, a cheerful, candy-like color combination that has made it a garden center staple. It reblooms readily over a long season from early to late summer, producing far more flowers per plant than older, single-bloom-cycle daylily varieties, and it is exceptionally easy to grow, tolerating a wide range of soil types and requiring little care beyond routine watering. The compact, well-branched scapes and reliable performance make it a favorite for mass plantings, borders, and low-maintenance landscaping. Divide congested clumps every three to four years in spring or fall to maintain vigor and bloom quality.

common_name: Siloam Double Classic Daylily (Ruffled Double Pink Miniature Daylily)

planting.note: Plant divisions in spring in well-drained, moderately fertile soil in full sun; Siloam Double Classic is part of the celebrated Siloam series of small-flowered daylilies bred by Pauline Henry, producing fully double, ruffled pink blooms on a compact plant.

directions: Plant in well-drained, moderately fertile soil in full sun. Siloam Double Classic is part of the renowned Siloam series of miniature and small-flowered daylilies bred by Pauline Henry of Siloam Springs, Arkansas, whose decades of breeding work produced some of the most refined small-flowered daylily cultivars available. Siloam Double Classic bears fully double, ruffled, rose-pink flowers with a deeper pink eye zone, on a compact plant well suited to smaller gardens, edging, and mass plantings where full-sized daylilies would be too large. Like other daylilies it is easy to grow in average soil with routine watering and tolerates heat well. Divide congested clumps every three to four years in spring or fall to maintain vigor and bloom quality.

common_name: Custard Candy Daylily (Cream-Yellow Ruffled Daylily with Rose Eye)

planting.note: Plant divisions in spring in well-drained, moderately fertile soil in full sun; Custard Candy is a popular reblooming daylily cultivar with creamy pale-yellow flowers marked by a rose-pink eye zone and matching ruffled edge, a soft companion to bolder-colored daylily cultivars.

directions: Plant in well-drained, moderately fertile soil in full sun. Custard Candy bears soft, creamy pale-yellow flowers accented with a rose-pink eye zone and a matching ruffled picotee edge, a gentle, pastel color combination that pairs well with the bolder reds, purples, and oranges of many other daylily cultivars in a mixed border. It reblooms readily over a long season from early to late summer, producing a steady supply of flowers, and is exceptionally easy to grow, tolerating a wide range of soil types and requiring little care beyond routine watering. The reliable, floriferous performance and soft coloring have made it a popular choice for both dedicated daylily collectors and casual gardeners. Divide congested clumps every three to four years in spring or fall to maintain vigor and bloom quality.
